description: On develop 01e69178a, `def f(xs :: [integer]), do: Enum.map(xs, fn x -> x + 1 end)` called with `[1, String.to_atom("a")]` passes the clause's run-time test (it asks only 'is a list'), and the body then reads every element as an integer: interp stops with 'internal error: an integer extern parameter received a non-integer after entry dispatch'; run panics in fz_ref_load_int (ExpectedTag expected 13 found 15). With a second clause `def f(_), do: :other` the call answers :ints instead of :other. Probe: scratchpad 4i4/deep2.fz and deeplist2.fz. A tuple annotation is tested per position ({:ok, :x} against {:ok, integer} goes to the next clause), so the hole is the list element. runtime_type_test_envelope keeps the element type (runtime_list_sig, src/compiler2/types/mod.rs:4631) while the emitted list question observes only list kind. Either the test walks the elements, or the type a passing value is narrowed to is what the test observed (a list), not the annotation. The same test serves fz-i89's spec-domain test, so a spec like @spec f([integer]) inherits the hole. Fails before, passes after: fixtures for both probes on interp, run and build. Acceptance: full gate green.
title: A list annotation's element type is trusted but never tested at run time
